blanks.sentence: Many people assume reading develops in the same way as speaking because it feels _____.
blanks.section: Reading is not simply built in

blanks.sentence: One mistaken assumption is that reading must be natural because it is a form of _____.
blanks.section: Reading is not simply built in

blanks.sentence: At birth, the brain already supports seeing and sound production through the _____.
blanks.section: Reading is not simply built in

blanks.sentence: However, babies do not already have the brain _____ needed for reading.
blanks.section: Reading is not simply built in

blanks.sentence: Evolution has not given humans a _____.
To read, the brain borrows areas used for vision, _____, language, attention and emotion.
Reading activates all _____ of the cortex.
Developing this ability can alter brain activity, structure and _____.
Reading Chinese symbols activates different brain areas from reading an _____.
Chinese characters place stronger demands on visual memory and _____.

multipleChoice.question: What point does Maryanne Wolf make about reading?
options: It develops automatically once children can speak.
It is easier than spoken language for most people.
It is not an ability that humans are naturally born to do.
It uses no connection with language.

multipleChoice.question: What do babies already have brain networks for?
options: Seeing and producing sounds.
Reading printed words fluently.
Understanding every language they hear.
Connecting symbols with abstract ideas.

multipleChoice.question: Why does the brain need to use existing systems when learning to read?
options: Reading requires only visual memory.
The cortex cannot change after childhood.
Spoken language prevents a reading network from forming.
There has not been enough evolutionary time for a separate reading brain.

multipleChoice.question: Which group of brain functions is mentioned as being recruited for reading?
options: Smell, balance, memory and movement.
Vision, sound processing, language and attention.
Hunger, emotion, sleep and breathing.
Pain response, touch, taste and imagination.

multipleChoice.question: How does Rebecca Gotlieb characterise reading overall?
options: A narrow skill handled by one small brain area.
A mainly mechanical process unrelated to identity.
A habit that changes only vocabulary knowledge.
A whole-brain process that can reshape who we are.

multipleChoice.question: What is one result of learning to read, according to the explanation?
options: It changes brain structure compared with not learning to read.
It removes the need for attention and language systems.
It makes all readers use identical brain circuits.
It prevents later changes in brain connectivity.

multipleChoice.question: What makes Chinese characters different from alphabetic writing in this discussion?
options: They represent only sounds and never ideas.
They are easier for stroke patients to read.
They use symbols rather than alphabet letters.
They do not require visual processing.

multipleChoice.question: What does the bilingual stroke case suggest?
options: Chinese and English must be stored in exactly the same brain areas.
Different writing systems can rely on different brain circuits.
A stroke normally improves alphabet reading.
People who read Chinese cannot read English after brain injury.

multipleChoice.question: Why does Maryanne Wolf mention the “requirements of Chinese”?
options: To argue that Chinese is less detailed than English.
To claim that alphabet systems use no memory.
To show that Chinese reading damages the circuit.
To explain why Chinese reading develops more visual memory and processing.

multipleChoice.question: What broader conclusion is supported by the final explanation of Chinese symbols?
options: The visual form of a writing system can shape brain development.
Detailed characters make reading impossible for bilingual people.
Alphabetic reading always produces stronger visual areas.
Brain circuits are fixed and unaffected by literacy.
